reports.concern: Certainty about availability during a delayed pickup
reports.claim: Assuming the interview sample represents evening readers, S1:O7 implies that an accurate availability answer could matter even when retrieval remains slow.
assumptions: The eight interviewed readers represent evening demand.

reports.concern: Reliable location records within preparation capacity
reports.claim: Assuming stale exception locations cause second searches, S1:O1 and S1:O3 imply location upkeep deserves priority; S1:O6 suggests that priority may exceed the preparation allowance.
assumptions: Corrections require clerk time comparable to the sampled day.

reports.concern: Meaning of the faster cart sample
reports.claim: Assuming cart pickups differ in arrival recency or volume, S1:O4 cannot establish that cart storage improves retrieval; it weakens any unconditional claim that shelf order is faster.
assumptions: The cart sample may differ from shelf pickups in recency or volume.

tension: Reader evidence points toward availability certainty; operational inference points toward costly location upkeep; the cart sample questions the storage assumption while leaving its causal interpretation unsettled. These implications compete for the same limited clerk time.
